parsed.explanation: The operative regime is defined by a national, universal-exposure measure: the May 2025/April 2025 laws restricting public-restroom access by birth sex, which reach every trans visitor in every transit space daily and carry state threat-framing ('harassment risk'). Compounding this, gender-identity hate-crime/discrimination protections were stripped in 2017 and are not in force, leaving thin recourse. A documented police torture-rape of a trans woman (custody-tier severity) with ~20-year impunity, though concluded in a landmark 2025 conviction, sits alongside rising recorded hate crimes affecting trans women. Mitigants: no criminalisation of trans identity, functioning courts that have ruled for trans people (2025 conviction; 2025 unconstitutionality ruling), legal gender-marker change available, and an improving healthcare-climate. No imprisonment or execution exposure is documented. Net: Elevated Risk, mid-band, above criminalising jurisdictions but clearly below acceptance-with-protections ones.

entry_documents.protection: Gender-marker change via judicial process (2016 ruling) permits documents matching identity for those with access; not visitor-specific.
entry_documents.interaction: Foreign passports govern entry; no border friction documented.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Police torture and sexual abuse of a trans woman documented; historical impunity spanned ~20 years.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: December 2025 conviction of three officers (17 years) — first-ever discrimination-motivated conviction; courts demonstrably can work for trans people.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Police custody is the point of documented trans-specific state violence; slow recourse shows courts working, eventually.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National restroom bans by birth sex (May 2025 law; April 2025 child-protection law) apply to all public facilities — a universal-exposure, tier-1 constraint including transit spaces; inclusive signage banned.
federal_state_facilities.protection: July 2025 court ruling against an anti-equality decree; regional-court advisory opinion cited against the law, but no operative reversal documented.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Restriction applies nationally and reaches visitors automatically at any facility use; censorship provisions broaden exposure for content-bearing travel.

care_services.exposure: Medication-supply concerns raised by community; pathologising 'transsexualism' classification briefly imposed in 2024.
care_services.protection: June 2024 removal of pathologising terminology; ministry affirmed gender identity not a disease; conversion therapy banned for medical professionals.
care_services.interaction: Health-insurance classification governs coverage; visitor emergency-care denial not documented.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: State framing of trans people as harassment risks via restroom law; public institutions described as contributing to anti-LGBTIQ discrimination; NGO foreign-funding law risks weaponisation against queer organising; TV host harassment of lesbian legislator.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Capital court struck down an anti-equality decree (2025).
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Legislative hostility interacts with rising hate crimes targeting trans women.

minors_guardians.exposure: April 2025 sexual-integrity law bars trans youth from identity-matching restrooms and enables censorship of identity/educational content; obscenity sentence raised.
minors_guardians.protection: Age-of-consent equality (2012); conversion-therapy ban protects minors.
minors_guardians.interaction: Travelling parent faces same facility bans as child; guardianship friction not documented.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Hate crimes rising, trans women most affected; recorded figures acknowledged as sub-registry; high trans-sex-work prevalence signals vulnerability, though resident-sphere.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Court conviction of police perpetrators; regional venue denial conviction; Pride marches annually since 1984/2002.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police both perpetrator (historically) and eventually prosecuted — recourse exists but is slow; no denominator to gauge rate.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No gender-identity anti-discrimination/hate-crime protection in force since 2017 repeal; no surgical remedy path for discrimination claims.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Functioning courts (conviction, unconstitutionality ruling, southern-city venue verdict); complainants can litigate and win.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Uncertainty whether 6506/8457 fully enacted and how the two 2025 laws interlock; hate-crime magnitude unresolved.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.55-C restricts hospital wards by marker; this jurisdiction's restroom ban is broader (all public facilities, all visitors) but otherwise no custody-placement rule is documented, and courts here show stronger pro-trans rulings. Net comparable, slightly below 0.55-C on breadth of exposure, slightly above on judicial behaviour.

0.45-D's registration database creates durable discovery; here no such surveillance exists, but the restroom law is a comparable universal exposure and hate-crime levels plus police-perpetrator history are worse than 0.45-D's harms. Sits above 0.45-D.

0.75-C has discretionary but ultimately respectful entry practice and functional tribunals; this jurisdiction imposes a hostile nationwide facility statute with stripped protections and documented police torture, materially worse. Sits clearly below 0.75-C.

0.35-B involves routine police identity-harassment of visitors with no working recourse; here police targeting is documented as one historic (now-prosecuted) case, identity is not criminalised, and courts operate for trans people. Clearly above 0.35-B.

parsed.synthesis: The combined regime couples a tier-1 universal-exposure measure — a nationwide birth-sex restroom ban reaching every visitor at every facility use, with explicit state threat-framing — against no gender-identity anti-discrimination or hate-crime statute in force. Against this stand real, operating protections: courts that convict police torturers, strike down anti-equality decrees, and sanction venue exclusion; healthcare guidance improving; no criminalisation of identity or expression; Pride and community infrastructure intact. Violence against trans women is documented and rising but lacks denominators, so it is treated as elevated background plus a severe police-custody case with delayed but eventual recourse. The exposure is continuous and state-imposed while remedies are slow and partial: mid-Elevated Risk, roughly 0.47.
